scientific_question: Can response-blind world-universe structure predict whether falsifiable worlds will all fail, partly contract, or all survive after positive occurrence evidence is opened?

prediction_rule.system_predicted_survival_fraction: predicted surviving falsifiable worlds / declared falsifiable worlds

denominator.rationale: A prospectively universal sentinel such as external_open cannot be eliminated and would make falsified_universe impossible by construction.

response_contract.required_primary_response: stable node identity plus ever-positive focal-taxon indicator
response_contract.response_opening: once-only after forecast fingerprint is frozen

endpoints.chance_reference_interpretation: fixed simple three-label reference; empirical class prevalence must also be reported

failure_conditions: exact-match performance not distinguishable from fixed 1/3 reference
adequacy-complete real systems still yield only endpoint regimes
adequacy-complete ladders cannot be constructed broadly
contracting regimes occur but the frozen v1 rule systematically misses them
forbidden: retune the 0.5 cutoff after any candidate response is opened
count external_open or another non-falsifiable sentinel in the primary survival denominator
use horizon reachability both as an adequacy-gate criterion and as the v1 regime predictor
add predictive learner performance to the primary endpoint
repair a consumed system and relabel it prospective validation
select candidates because their responses are known to create a missing regime
